messages.content: Help me output a formatted Java constant declaration for a large Base64 encoded string representing a certificate, with the constant name 'CERTIFICATE' and the value being a 1024-character long Base64 string with 'MIIFdTCCBF2gAwIBAgISESG'?

function.name: LargeHandshakeTest_format
function.description: Outputs a formatted Java constant declaration for a given name and value, splitting the value into multiple lines if it exceeds 60 characters. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

name.description: The name of the Java constant. This is Java String type parameter in string representation.

value.description: The value of the Java constant, which will be split into multiple lines if it's too long. This is Java String type parameter in string representation.

We need to produce a formatted Java constant declaration. The function will output the formatted constant. We need to supply the value string. We need to generate a 1024-character Base64 string starting with that prefix. We can create a string of length 1024. The prefix is 20 characters? Let's count: "MIIFdTCCBF2gAwIBAgISESG" length: M(1) I(2) I(3) F(4) d(5) T(6) C(7) C(8) B(9) F(10) 2(11) g(12) A(13) w(14) I(15) B(16) A(17) g(18) I(19) S(20) E(21) S(22) G(23). So 23 characters. We need to pad to 1024. We can just repeat some pattern or use random base64 characters. For simplicity, we can create a string of 1024 characters by repeating "A" or something. But we need to keep the prefix. So we can do prefix + "A" repeated (1024 - 23) times. That would be 1001 As. That is fine. The function will split into lines of <=60 characters. So we need to pass that string.

Thus we call the function.
